template.name: Spring Boot
template.description: Spring Boot web service — Kotlin or Java, Gradle or Maven, JDK 17 or 21.
param.artifactId.label: Artifact ID
param.artifactId.help: Project identifier, follows the project name
param.packageName.label: Package name
param.packageName.help: Application package, follows the artifact (e.g. com.example.demoapi)
param.groupId.label: Group ID
param.groupId.help: Publisher coordinates, derived from the package
param.version.label: Version
param.langage.label: Language
param.langage.choix.kotlin.sousTitre: Kotlin sources with the Spring (all-open) plugin
param.langage.choix.java.sousTitre: Plain Java sources, without the Kotlin plugin
param.buildSystem.label: Build system
param.buildSystem.choix.maven.sousTitre: pom.xml with the Spring Boot parent
param.jdkVersion.label: JDK version
param.jdkVersion.help: LTS version fully validated by CodeIDE
param.includeJpa.label: Spring Data JPA
param.includeJpa.help: Entity and Spring Data repository backed by H2 (the in-memory repository is replaced)
param.includeSecurity.label: Spring Security
param.includeSecurity.help: Explicit SecurityFilterChain (401 without credentials, HTTP Basic)
param.includeActuator.label: Actuator
param.includeActuator.help: Exposes /actuator/health (open without authentication when Security is on)
param.includeValidation.label: Validation
param.includeValidation.help: Validated DTO (Bean Validation) on POST /salutations + invalid-case test
param.includeTests.label: Tests
param.includeTests.help: Spring context test, service test and tests of the options you ticked
param.includeWrapper.label: Gradle Wrapper
param.includeWrapper.help: Includes gradlew with a pinned, checksummed distribution (Gradle only)
preset.api-rest.description: Sets JPA (H2) and Validation for a complete REST API
hint.jpa.kotlin.maven: JPA with Kotlin on Maven: the no-arg (jpa) compiler is configured in the generated pom.xml.
salutation.kdoc: Greeting returned by the API — identifier and message.
depot.kdoc: Greeting repository port — both implementations realize it.
depot.memoire.kdoc: In-memory repository — lightweight variant without persistence.
depot.jpa.kdoc: Spring Data JPA repository — persists greetings into H2.
depot.entites.kdoc: Spring Data access to the entities, ordered by identifier.
entite.kdoc: JPA entity persisted in H2 (salutations table).
dto.kdoc: Body expected by POST /salutations — the name is required.
securite.kdoc: Spring Security configuration — explicit filter chain.
securite.chaine.kdoc: Protected API (401 without credentials, HTTP Basic); /actuator/health left open when Actuator is ticked.
controller.greet.kdoc: Greets the name given in the request (the world when absent).
controller.salutations.kdoc: Records a greeting and returns its identifier.
service.kdoc: Greeting service — testable core, independent from persistence.
test.kdoc: Covers the greeting service without starting Spring (in-memory test double).
test.name: Edsger
test.historique: Checks that the service records and lists greetings.
tests.kdoc: Checks that the Spring context starts.
test.validation.kdoc: Checks the DTO Bean Validation constraint (name required).
test.securite.kdoc: Checks that the API answers 401 without credentials and that /actuator/health stays open when requested.
readme.description: Spring Boot web service generated by CodeIDE.
readme.maven.note: Maven 3.9+ installed (no Maven wrapper is included — use your local installation).
readme.dep.jpa: Spring Data JPA — relational persistence with H2
readme.dep.jpa.detail: Spring Data JPA — Salutation entity + repository persisted in H2 (in-memory database jdbc:h2:mem:salutations)
readme.dep.security: Spring Security — HTTP Basic (user « user », password logged at startup)
readme.dep.validation: Validation — POST /salutations body validated (Bean Validation, 400 when the name is empty)
readme.securite: Spring Security is active: endpoints answer 401 without credentials (user « user », generated password shown at startup).
readme.profils.defaut: active by default, to switch to
